description.short_caption: Chest CT showing bilateral lung abnormalities and pleural effusion.
description.detailed_description: This axial chest CT image demonstrates significant abnormalities in both lungs. There are areas of consolidation and ground-glass opacities, particularly in the lower lobes. A large pleural effusion is visible on the left side, causing compression of the adjacent lung tissue. The mediastinum appears shifted slightly to the right, likely due to the effusion. No intravenous contrast is evident in this scan.

description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing bilateral lung fields and mediastinal structures.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph showing the thoracic cavity, including the lungs, heart, and bony structures such as the ribs and spine. The lung fields appear symmetric, and the mediastinum is centrally located. No obvious consolidation, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax is visible. The image is labeled with 'L' to indicate the left side.

description.short_caption: Chest CT showing bilateral cavitary lung lesions.
description.detailed_description: This axial chest CT image demonstrates bilateral cavitary lesions in the lungs, with areas of consolidation and air-fluid levels. The findings are suggestive of necrotizing pneumonia or abscess formation. The mediastinal structures appear midline, and there is no obvious pleural effusion. The image is in soft tissue window settings.
